newsitem.title: UK: Corporate backers raise share of Lloyd's capacity.
newsitem.headline: Corporate backers raise share of Lloyd's capacity.

text.p: The Lloyd's of London insurance market said Tuesday its underwriting capacity for 1997 would be 10.3 billion British pounds ($17.16 billion), and that corporate backers would provide a bigger portion of that than in 1996.

Capacity, the amount Lloyd's can underwrite in terms of premium income, is based on the amount investors are willing to subscribe to the market each year. Capacity in 1996 was 10 billion pounds ($16.66 billion).
Investors consist of individuals, known as Names, and corporate backers.
The number of Names investing in Lloyd's will fall next year to 9,972 from 12,798 in 1996, and individual members will supply 5.8 billion pounds ($9.66 billion), or 56 percent of the capacity.
The balance of 4.5 billion pounds ($7.5 billion), or 44 percent of the capacity, will be supplied by a total of 202 corporate and other limited liability members.
The Names are still the majority investors in Lloyd's but are declining in number. They provided 70 percent, and corporate members 30 percent of this year's capacity.
The insurance market has seen an increasing shift toward corporate backers after a series of unprecedented natural disasters and liability claims brought massive losses for individual members.
Lloyd's in September completed a 3.2 billion pound ($5 billion) rescue plan, under which billions of dollars in past liabilities were reinsured by a new company, Equitas.
